objective: Polish the existing V11.4 desktop HTML proposal presentation so wide/desktop viewports feel intentionally composed and premium, while preserving the canonical proposal content, data semantics, existing mobile behavior, PDF behavior, and runtime architecture.
scope: Inspect the current canonical proposal HTML renderer and its existing responsive CSS/layout.
Make the minimum bounded presentation changes needed for a polished desktop/wide-screen experience.
Prefer CSS/layout/responsive changes over data-model, route, renderer-architecture, or content changes.
Keep the current mobile presentation behavior intact unless a shared rule must be adjusted to prevent a regression.
Use existing repository regression/validation commands relevant to HTML proposal presentation and responsive behavior.
Record exact changed files, commands/tests, evidence, warnings, and blockers in gt63/bridge/result.json.
doNot: merge, deploy, push to production, or create release/tag
change proposal business data, pricing, hotel/flight facts, or canonical content semantics
introduce a second proposal renderer or fork HOME/PDF/client HTML into divergent presentation sources
perform unrelated refactors or dependency upgrades
claim visual or regression validation that was not actually performed
acceptanceCriteria: Desktop/wide HTML presentation is visibly more intentional and premium than the current baseline.
No horizontal overflow, broken cards, clipped text, or obviously stretched mobile-only composition at representative desktop widths.
Existing mobile layout remains usable and materially unchanged in behavior.
Canonical proposal content and runtime semantics are preserved.
Relevant existing deterministic regression/validation suites pass, or any pre-existing/unrelated failure is reported exactly and fail-closed.
Only bounded files necessary for the responsive polish plus gt63/bridge/result.json are changed.
No merge/deploy occurs; final acceptance remains a Human Gate.
expectedEvidence: before/after or equivalent rendered desktop evidence if the environment supports it
